message.content: Lions mate during a brief but intense courtship period that typically lasts only a few days. During this time, a male will approach a female who is in estrus (the fertile phase of her cycle). He may display dominance through vocalizations, scent marking, and physical displays such as roaring or showing his mane. If the female accepts, they will engage in copulation, which can last from a few minutes up to an hour. After mating, the female usually remains with the male’s pride until she gives birth, after which she may leave to raise her cubs alone.
